segments: Docker Swarm is Docker's native cluster orchestration solution. It provides service orchestration integrated with Docker tooling and uses a subset of legacy Compose v3 rather than the full current Compose specification. It suits small teams and single-cluster deployments.

The following is only an example for a planned test cluster. Inter-node management/overlay communication and firewall policies are required, and managers should be planned around quorum requirements. Join tokens are sensitive credentials and must be transferred securely. Replace the documentation addresses with reachable node addresses.
Stack Deploy: migrate compatible Compose v3 configuration

Common service fields can be reused, but stack deploy uses legacy Compose v3. Modern features such as develop/watch/profiles and build cannot be migrated directly. Build images ahead of time and publish them to a registry accessible to all nodes.

Key point: Sharing a file works only for compatible fields. First inspect the output and warnings from docker stack config, then check images, secret/config sources, networks, placement, and volumes. Success with single-host Compose does not prove that cluster deployment behavior is correct.
File injection supported; protecting the source is your responsibility
Swarm secrets provide encrypted Raft storage and distribution

Ingress network: Accessing port 80 on any node automatically routes the request to a healthy replica of the web service. The routing mesh provides ingress forwarding; external load balancing, TLS, and healthy-traffic policies may still be needed.
When should you move from Swarm to K8s?
Growing scale with ecosystem, scheduling, or governance requirements
Evaluate Kubernetes against your operational capabilities; there is no fixed node-count threshold
A team with existing K8s experience

Tool selection depends on availability, scheduling, governance, and team capabilities. Swarm builds on Docker service operations, while Kubernetes offers different controllers and an ecosystem of its own. Learning time cannot be guaranteed in a fixed number of minutes or weeks.

The Docker and Podman learning paths eventually converge on K8s. Whichever engine you use to build images and run local tests, production can still remain on a single host or use another orchestrator. Whether to adopt Kubernetes depends on your requirements.

Swarm scheduling can recreate tasks after a node failure, but a local volume does not automatically replicate its data to another node. Data services need shared storage, replication, or explicit placement and recovery plans. Losing a majority quorum of managers affects scheduling and management. Rolling-update settings such as start-first, health checks, and failure_action do not guarantee reversible database migrations or uninterrupted traffic. Removing a stack stops its services; check the lifecycle of each volume and external secret/config separately.
